sources.citation: Harley, Matthew. 2020. Aspects of the phonology and morphosyntax of Kyak, an Adamawa language of Nigeria. Language in Africa 1(3): 373-404. doi:10.37892/2686-8946-2020-1-3-373-404
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online (also online with a university library login)
sources.note: Describes the sister lect KYAK [bka], said (p. 377) to be with Moo and Leelau 'dialects of the same language' linguistically (>90% lexical similarity). Sec. 3.3 Tones pp. 378-379: three contrastive lexical tones H, L, Falling, downstep; sec. 3.4 vowel length not contrastive. No mention of stress anywhere.
